title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 57-60 of the notes). K is a base field (characteristic 0, possibly C). L/K is a function field with fixed algebraic closure \bar L. E_L^{\bar L} is the Galois group of L, or an arithmetic fundamental group of Spec L relative to K. A place x' of \bar L lies above a discrete valuation ring V = O_x of L. Write K̃_x for the henselized fraction field, Ũ_x = Spec K̃_x, and S̃_x = Spec O^h_x for the henselian trait. The previous page records the standard isomorphisms N_{x'} ≅ π1(Ũ_x) (decomposition group) and I_{x'} = ker(π1(Ũ_x) → π1(S̃_x) = Gal(\overline{k(x)}/k(x))) (inertia).

This page. A model U of L/K (a normal variety with function field L) gives a quotient E_U^{\bar L} = π1(U, \bar L) of E_L. The composite N_{x'} → E_L → E_U is the map π1(Ũ_x) → π1(U) induced by Ũ_x → U.

(1) Easy direction. If Ũ_x → U extends to S̃_x, i.e. the valuation has its centre in U, then π1(Ũ_x) → π1(U) factors through π1(S̃_x). So I_{x'} maps trivially to π1(U): no ramification at a point lying in U.

(2) Converse (bracketed question). Grothendieck asks 'Et la réciproque ?'. The marginal note says it should hold provided there are 'enough' factorisations through curves of a certain elementary type, apparently (0,3) or (1,1), i.e. the hyperbolic building blocks. It also seems to say: after passing to a finite étale cover U' of U dominating a suitable model. He marks it 'à garder !'.

(3) Proper model. Suppose U is an open subset of a proper model X. By the valuative criterion of properness, V has a centre a on X. In the dimension-1 (codim-1) situation he asserts that the necessary and sufficient condition for I_{x'} → E_U to be trivial is a ∈ U.

Purpose. The next page then recovers π1(U) as E_L divided by the closed normal subgroup generated by the inertia groups I_V of the divisorial valuations V = O_{U,x} centred at codim-1 points of U. This is Zariski-Nagata purity, the Galois-theoretic description of π1(U) inside Gal(L). It feeds into the 'Riemann-Zariski space' 𝒳_{L/K} = lim of proper models introduced next.
errors: The claimed NSC 'I_{x'} → π1(U) trivial iff a ∈ U' is false without extra hypotheses. Example: U = A^1_K ⊂ P^1 with a = ∞; the geometric π1 of A^1 is trivial in characteristic 0, so the inertia at ∞ dies although a ∉ U. Example: U = P^2 minus a line; π1(U) is trivial, so the inertia of the boundary divisor dies. Grothendieck's own marginal remark (need for 'enough' maps to (0,3)/(1,1)-type curves, or passage to a cover U') shows he was aware the converse requires a hyperbolicity-type hypothesis. The final sentence on the page overstates it, unless 'dim 1' refers to a restricted hyperbolic setting.

ideas.what: Inertia of a valuation centred in U maps trivially to π1(U).
ideas.modern_name: Unramifiedness of covers at points of U; specialization of π1 for henselian traits

ideas.what: π1(U) is the quotient of Gal(L) by the closed normal subgroup generated by the inertia groups of codim-1 points of U.
ideas.modern_name: Zariski-Nagata purity of the branch locus
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. X §3; SGA2 Exp. X

ideas.what: Converse: inertia of a boundary divisorial valuation survives in π1(U) if U has enough maps to hyperbolic curves of type (0,3)/(1,1), possibly after a finite étale cover.
ideas.modern_name: Faithfulness of boundary inertia in π1 of hyperbolic varieties / good (elementary anabelian) neighbourhoods
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (anabelian letter to Faltings 1983, Esquisse); later Mochizuki, Tamagawa, Nakamura on inertia in anabelian geometry
ideas.where_published: Spirit close to the Esquisse d'un programme (anabelian elementary varieties) and the Faltings letter; this exact formulation not known to me

ideas.what: Using the valuative criterion of properness to locate the centre of a valuation on a proper model, as a precursor to the Riemann-Zariski space.

missed.claim: Grothendieck conjectures a converse to purity: the image of boundary inertia in π1(U) is nontrivial (faithful), provided there are 'enough' maps from U, or from a finite étale cover of U, to curves of type (0,3) or (1,1). This amounts to a criterion for the survival of divisorial inertia in hyperbolic/anabelian varieties. It is related to later results on inertia groups in anabelian geometry, but stated here as an open question to 'keep'.
missed.quote: [Et la réciproque ? Ça devrait être le cas pourvu qu'il y ait "suffisamment" ... du type (0,3) ou (1,1) ... à garder !]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Gives an early Grothendieck formulation linking boundary-inertia faithfulness to elementary (0,3)/(1,1) fibrations. This is a minor historical datum for anabelian geometry; the mathematical content is largely known (e.g. good-neighbourhood arguments, Mochizuki/Tamagawa on decomposition groups).

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly standard purity and inertia bookkeeping. The only notable detail is the marginal hint tying the converse to (0,3)/(1,1)-type maps, which is consistent with Grothendieck's known anabelian ideas, and the reading of that hint is uncertain.
transcription_corrections: Margin: '(0,0) ou (0,1)' is likely '(0,3) ou (1,1)' (uncertain); the word before it may be 'fibrations' or 'factorisations' rather than 'éléments'.
The final line plausibly reads '(par définition, critère valuatif de la propreté) que V a un centre a sur X' and '(NB on peut ...)'.
'et [?] homom.' plausibly 'et ce dernier homom. est nul' or similar; 'I_{x'}' is inserted above 'est le noyau de', i.e. 'puisque I_{x'} est le noyau de E_{Ũ_x} → E_{S̃_x}'.
